title: Dilip Goswami (Dharma and Management) — Incorruptible as a blueprint for a dharmic company
summary: Dilip Goswami — deep tech founder and executive coach — sets out to write his own essay on how to build a dharmic company and, after reading Incorruptible, ends up writing a book review instead, distilling Eric's argument that a founder's values alone can't be the load-bearing structure for the long-term character of a company.
blockquote: Eric illustrates through a remarkable range of stories, both from history and from the modern day, that a founder's values can not be the only load-bearing structure for the long-term character of a company. This structure has to be designed with the same seriousness with which one designs a product. And it has to be designed against something — against the gravity that will act on every successor, every future board, every future financial cycle.
blockquote_source: Dilip Goswami on LinkedIn (linking to his Dharma and Management essay)
